entity_identifiers: MDALL licence number (original_licence_no) - the authoritative Canadian product-licence id
company_id (MDALL's own company identifier, resolvable via /company/?company_name=)
device identifier via /deviceidentifier/ - takes a real UDI-DI, i.e. an official DI bridge
UNKNOWN - no FDA 510(k)/PMA number, and no EU SRN/Basic UDI-DI
historical_coverage: all Class II-IV licences currently or formerly held (active + archived states). Class I devices need no licence and are absent by design, as are Investigational Testing Authorisations and Special Access records
known_limitations: last_refresh_dt is a database refresh stamp; using it as a publication date would make every licence look freshly published on the last refresh day
end_date is a cancellation date. The collection protocol forbids using an expiry/cancellation date as the first-publication date, and it is future-dated for active-looking rows
MDALL publishes no per-record publication timestamp, so source_public_at can only be a derived proxy from first_licence_status_dt / first_licence_dt (flag quality=derived)
Class I devices are absent by regulation, so Canada under-covers low-risk devices

the /company/ search is a %LIKE% match: 'MEDTRONIC' returns 29 companies (incl. unrelated subsidiaries), 'PHILIPS' 31, so company linkage must go through the alias index and stay a candidate where the alias layer is unsure
the deviceidentifier bridge exists but is sparse: the sampled US-only Medtronic DI had no MDALL row, so it only resolves devices actually licensed in Canada
licence: Open Government Licence - Canada (open.canada.ca CKAN record for the MDALL dataset, verified)
rate_limits: no documented numeric limit; the unfiltered ?state=active dumps are large (the device dump did not complete inside a 120 s timeout from this host), so queries should be scoped by company_id / licence_number / device_identifier. We paced at 1.0 s
research_value: Canada is the one market where an official endpoint resolves a UDI-DI to a national product licence, giving a genuine second-country anchor for the same device and a first_licence date that is independent of FDA's decision clock. The documented JSON API (no key, no session) also makes MDALL far cheaper to collect than the EU or UK registers.
source_name: Health Canada Medical Devices Active Licence Listing (MDALL) API
timestamp_fields: first_licence_status_dt (licence level - date the licence was first issued)
first_licence_dt (device level - date the device was added to the licence)
last_refresh_dt (database refresh stamp - NOT a publication date)
update_frequency: daily (CKAN metadata states frequency P1D); each licence row carries last_refresh_dt
